name: Bardot Plastics
old_description: Three generations of expertise delivering precision parts since 1973. Our modern facility with state-of-the-art equipment ensures quality at every step.
about:
Bardot Plastics operates from a modern facility in Easton, Pennsylvania, where it has been manufacturing precision injection-molded parts since 1973. The company was founded by J. Lee Boucher and remains a third-generation family business, now led by his sons Chris, Jim, and Rick Boucher. What began as a vision for superior injection molding has grown into a full-service operation built on the principle of “making it right the first time.”

The shop specializes in large-tonnage molding, running presses up to 1,760 tons to produce large, complex components that many molders cannot accommodate. Its end-to-end capabilities cover design consultation, integrated tooling (single-cavity, multi-cavity, and family molds), insert molding, sonic welding, sub-assembly, and in-house packaging and fulfillment. A 120-ton central chilling unit and robotic part-removal systems support consistent quality across prototype and high-volume runs, working with both engineered and non-engineered resins.

Bardot serves a diverse industrial base including office furniture, lawn and garden, waste and recycling, industrial equipment, military, construction, agricultural, and commercial markets. Customers rely on the company for ergonomic workplace components, durable industrial parts, military-spec precision pieces, weather-resistant outdoor products, structural components, and agricultural parts built to withstand harsh environments.

The company differentiates itself through continuous technology investment — exemplified by the recent chilling unit installation — and a single-point-of-contact project management model. Its guiding principles of excellence, innovation, sustainability, and partnership reflect a heritage of delivering tight tolerances and dimensional stability regardless of part size or complexity.
